buildcraftcore/item/gear_wood: Every machine starts somewhere. Yours starts with a couple of sticks and a gear that probably won't survive much strain.
The Wooden Gear is the first step toward BuildCraft machinery. Upgrade it to craft stronger gears and many other components.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Craft Wooden Gears in planned batches. Higher-tier gears consume the previous tier, so keep a few lower-tier spares for machines and tools.
buildcraftcore/item/gear_stone: Wooden teeth are fine until a machine has actual work to do. A little stone should help.
The Stone Gear is crafted from a Wooden Gear and provides the basis for sturdier machinery.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Craft Stone Gears in planned batches. Higher-tier gears consume the previous tier, so keep a few lower-tier spares for machines and tools.
buildcraftcore/item/gear_iron: A stone gear can only take so much punishment. For engines and heavy machinery, it is time to work with iron.
The Iron Gear upgrades a Stone Gear and is used in more advanced BuildCraft machines.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Craft Iron Gears in planned batches. Higher-tier gears consume the previous tier, so keep a few lower-tier spares for machines and tools.
buildcraftcore/item/gear_gold: When a mechanism calls for precision rather than brute strength, gold starts looking surprisingly useful.
The Gold Gear is crafted from an Iron Gear and is used in advanced machines and components.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Craft Gold Gears in planned batches. Higher-tier gears consume the previous tier, so keep a few lower-tier spares for machines and tools.
buildcraftcore/item/gear_diamond: You've reached the point where even gold gears are not quite enough. Luckily, you brought diamonds.
The Diamond Gear is the highest-tier gear and an ingredient in some of BuildCraft's most advanced machines.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Craft Diamond Gears in planned batches. Higher-tier gears consume the previous tier, so keep a few lower-tier spares for machines and tools.
buildcraftcore/item/wrench: Machines are much easier to live with when rotating one does not require a pickaxe and a complete reinstallation.
The BuildCraft Wrench rotates and reconfigures supported machines and pipes. The exact click action depends on the target.

Hint: By default, items in c:tools/wrench can perform supported BuildCraft wrench interactions; useWrenchTag controls this compatibility. Some targets use a Wrench to change a mode or remove an installed module. Read the target page before using it on a finished setup.
buildcraftcore/item/paintbrush: A splash of color looks nice. On a pipe network, the right color can also keep two lines from connecting.
Paintbrushes apply one of the sixteen Minecraft dye colors to compatible blocks. Most blocks only change appearance, but differently colored pipes do not connect to one another.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Keep separate brushes for permanent pipe networks. Coloring only the branches that must not connect is usually easier to maintain than coloring every pipe.
buildcraftcore/item/marker_connector: Large work areas become much easier to manage when their laser boxes can be adjusted without rebuilding every marker.
The Marker Connector links compatible markers and directly edits Volume Box and Path Marker geometry.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Marker reach is configured in the Balance settings for Markers; the default maximum distance is 64 blocks. A visible marker can still be outside the permitted connection range.

For Land Marks and Path Marks, aim at the candidate connection between compatible markers and use the Connector to link them. Arrange Land Marks on matching axes and Path Marks in the intended travel order.

For a Volume Box, aim at a corner and right-click to begin moving it, then right-click again to confirm. Sneak-right-click while editing cancels the edit. Sneak-right-click an unlocked box to remove it.

An installed Filler Planner has its own corner interaction: use the Connector on the add-on to open its settings; sneak-use the add-on to remove it. A machine can lock a Volume Box while using it.
buildcraftcore/item/marker_path: Straight lines are useful, but large projects often need a route that bends around terrain and machinery.
Path Marks define an ordered route for machines that support path-based work.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Test a short Builder path before extending it. A path is an ordered series of construction positions, not a robot work-area whitelist.

Place Path Marks at the points the route should pass through. Use the Marker Connector to link them in order. The visible laser line shows the path that a compatible Builder or other machine will follow.

A path is directional: the order in which marks are linked determines the order of the points. Break or reconnect marks to reshape the route.

Place a compatible Builder beside the connected path and follow the Builder instructions for its stored schematic. Path positions determine where the Builder repeats its construction.

A Map Location can record a Path Mark network for consumers that explicitly accept paths. Robot work areas use an area or painted zone; a path alone does not define all blocks that a worker may change.
buildcraftcore/item/list: Nine filter slots are not much help when a sorting system must recognize an entire workshop of related materials.
A List stores reusable item-matching rules for compatible pipe filters, Gate parameters and robot controls.

<bold>Hint:</bold> Check the receiving action page before using a List. A List works in supported work/tool filters, but it is not a universal replacement for a station item sample or a worker block sample.

Hold the List and right-click to open its editor. Name it and place reference items into its two rows of phantom slots; the real items are not consumed.

In normal mode, each row can hold up to nine accepted samples. Exact Match includes stored item data such as names and enchantments. Leave it off when worn tools or differently named items should still match.

Match Variants and Match Equivalents use the first sample of the row to describe a broader group. Enabling either clears the additional editable samples in that row; the remaining slots show example matches. With both enabled, matching uses the broadest supported class grouping. The available groups depend on the item and installed integrations.

Put the configured List into a filter that supports Lists, or copy it into a compatible Gate parameter. Stored Gate parameters are snapshots: editing the List in your hand does not revise a copy already stored in a Gate. Copy it into the parameter again after making changes.

For robot logistics, a Work Filter can match cargo items and a Tool Filter can match supplied tools. Station Provide/Accept/Request actions and block-search careers have their own parameter rules; use their documented item or block samples. An empty List contains no accepted samples.
buildcraftcore/block/engine_wood: A piston that runs on redstone alone? It may not be powerful, but it is a remarkably convenient start.
The Redstone Engine is BuildCraft's smallest MJ engine. It runs on redstone without burning any fuel.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Use a Redstone Engine to power small extraction devices directly. It cannot feed a Kinesis Pipe network.

With the default balance, a running Redstone Engine generates up to 0.05 MJ/t. Point it directly at a compatible low-power consumer, such as a Wooden extraction pipe, and apply redstone. It does not feed Kinesis Pipes; use a stronger engine for a power network.

Normal engine heat stages are Blue, Green, Yellow, Red and <bold>Overheat</bold>. Black belongs to the Creative Engine. The Redstone Engine regulates itself below Overheat and cannot explode from heat.

It needs a redstone signal and a compatible direct consumer. Rotate it with a Wrench to aim the moving end. Rate displays can show MJ per tick or per second; the display unit does not change the actual output.
buildcraftcore/trigger/always_on: Sometimes you simply need an action to stay enabled.
Always On is a Gate trigger that remains active regardless of neighboring blocks or signals.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Use Always On for an action that should remain enabled without a redstone clock.
buildcraftcore/trigger/redstone_active: Is the pipe receiving redstone power?
Redstone Signal On is a Gate trigger that checks incoming redstone power.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Enable Gate Side Only when you want to monitor the face carrying the Gate rather than all sides of its pipe.

The trigger is active when the pipe receives a redstone signal on any monitored side.

This is the pipe input, not the work state or inventory contents of a neighboring machine.

With no side restriction, the trigger checks the pipe redstone input as a whole. Select Gate Side Only in a supported trigger parameter slot to check only the physical face carrying the Gate. A Lapis modifier can supply this trigger parameter.
buildcraftcore/trigger/redstone_inactive: Is the pipe free of redstone input?
Redstone Signal Off is a Gate trigger that checks incoming redstone power.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Enable Gate Side Only when you want to monitor the face carrying the Gate rather than all sides of its pipe.

The trigger is active when the pipe receives no redstone signal on the monitored sides.

This is the pipe input, not the work state or inventory contents of a neighboring machine.

buildcraftcore/trigger/inventory_empty: Inventory Empty is a Gate trigger available when the pipe is next to a compatible inventory.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Inventories may expose different slots from different faces. Place the Gate on the pipe facing the inventory you want to inspect.

The trigger is active when the inventory slots exposed toward the pipe contain no items. If that face exposes no item slots at all, the trigger is unavailable or false; a blocked connection is not an empty chest.
If the pipe touches multiple compatible blocks, the Gate can offer separate triggers for each side. The trigger icon indicates which side is being checked.
buildcraftcore/trigger/inventory_contain: Does the adjacent inventory contain an item?
Items in Inventory is a Gate trigger available when the pipe is next to a compatible inventory.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Inventories may expose different slots from different faces. Place the Gate on the pipe facing the inventory you want to inspect.

With no filter, the trigger is active when any exposed slot contains an item. With a sample or supported List, at least one matching item must be present. The sample count is not a requested quantity.

Copy an item or a configured List into the trigger parameter to select matching contents. Clear the parameter to check for any item. If you need a stock threshold rather than simple presence, use an Inventory Below trigger.
If the pipe touches multiple compatible blocks, the Gate can offer separate triggers for each side. The trigger icon indicates which side is being checked.
buildcraftcore/trigger/inventory_space: Does the adjacent inventory have room for more items?
Space in Inventory is a Gate trigger available when the pipe is next to a compatible inventory.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Inventories may expose different slots from different faces. Place the Gate on the pipe facing the inventory you want to inspect.

The trigger checks whether there is any available slot capacity. It does not promise space for a whole stack. With a specific item sample, it also checks whether at least one of that item can actually be inserted through the monitored face.

Use a specific item sample when checking a filtered machine input. An empty parameter or a List gives a generic physical-space check; a List does <bold>not</bold> prove that one of its entries passes the inventory insertion rules.

The sample is copied and not consumed. A full stack on the cursor still tests for room for one item, not room for that entire stack.
If the pipe touches multiple compatible blocks, the Gate can offer separate triggers for each side. The trigger icon indicates which side is being checked.
buildcraftcore/trigger/inventory_full: Inventory Full is a Gate trigger available when the pipe is next to a compatible inventory.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Inventories may expose different slots from different faces. Place the Gate on the pipe facing the inventory you want to inspect.

The trigger is active when all exposed slots have reached their effective item limits. An inventory with no exposed slots is not treated as full.

For a machine that rejects one particular item while still having other empty slots, use Space in Inventory with that item sample; generic fullness does not describe every insertion rule.
If the pipe touches multiple compatible blocks, the Gate can offer separate triggers for each side. The trigger icon indicates which side is being checked.
buildcraftcore/trigger/inventory_below_2: Is the adjacent inventory less than 25% full?
Below 25% is a Gate trigger that checks the fill level of a connected inventory.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Leave the filter empty to measure total inventory fill. An item filter checks matching stacks; Lists work only with inventories that support filtering.

The trigger is active when the counted items occupy strictly less than 25% of their counted capacity. It is not active at exactly 25%. Without a sample, it measures the exposed inventory; with a sample it counts matching stacks and capacity that can accept that item.

Use a single item sample for predictable stock checks. Matching occupied slots contribute their effective stack limits; compatible empty slots contribute the amount they can accept.

A List can identify matching occupied stacks, but counting empty capacity for a List requires a compatible filtered inventory. A List on an ordinary chest is therefore not a reliable percentage-of-chest measurement.

buildcraftcore/trigger/fluid_empty: Tank Empty is a Gate trigger available when the pipe is next to a compatible fluid handler.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Fluid tanks may expose different connections from different faces. Check which side of the tank the Gate is monitoring.
The trigger is active when the adjacent fluid handler contains no fluid.

buildcraftcore/trigger/fluid_contains: Does the adjacent tank contain fluid?
Fluid in Tank is a Gate trigger available when the pipe is next to a compatible fluid handler.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Fluid tanks may expose different connections from different faces. Check which side of the tank the Gate is monitoring.
The trigger is active when the tank contains any matching fluid.

Copy a filled fluid container into the parameter to select that fluid. Clear the parameter to accept any contained fluid. An empty bucket does not select water or another fluid. Temperature variants can be distinct fluids; use the intended filled container.
If the pipe touches multiple compatible blocks, the Gate can offer separate triggers for each side. The trigger icon indicates which side is being checked.
buildcraftcore/trigger/fluid_space: Can the adjacent tank accept more fluid?
Space in Tank is a Gate trigger available when the pipe is next to a compatible fluid handler.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Fluid tanks may expose different connections from different faces. Check which side of the tank the Gate is monitoring.

Without a sample, this checks for an empty or partly filled tank. With a filled-container sample, it asks whether the selected fluid can actually be inserted through the monitored face. It tests for any accepted amount, not an entire bucket.

Use a filled bucket or another supported filled container for the fluid you intend to deliver. An empty bucket carries no fluid sample and falls back to the generic capacity check. The real container is not consumed.
If the pipe touches multiple compatible blocks, the Gate can offer separate triggers for each side. The trigger icon indicates which side is being checked.

<bold>Hint:</bold> Fluid tanks may expose different connections from different faces. Check which side of the tank the Gate is monitoring.

buildcraftcore/trigger/fluid_below_25: Is the adjacent tank less than 25% full?
Below 25% is a Gate trigger that checks the fill level of a connected tank.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Leave the parameter empty to check the available tank. A filled container selects a particular fluid for the level check.

The trigger is active when at least one eligible tank is strictly below 25% full. For a handler with several tanks, this is a per-tank check, not the sum of all tanks. An eligible empty tank also satisfies it.

Copy a filled fluid container into the parameter to select its fluid. A matching tank is checked at its own capacity; an empty tank is eligible when the handler can accept the selected fluid. Leave the parameter empty to inspect any available tank.

buildcraftcore/trigger/engine_blue: Is the nearby engine in the blue heat stage?
Engine Blue is a Gate trigger for the blue stage of a connected engine.

buildcraftcore/trigger/machine_active: Does the machine still have work to do?
Has Work checks the work state of an adjacent compatible machine.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Has Work is a job indicator, not a power meter. A machine may have pending work while waiting for materials, output space or an enable condition.

The trigger reports the work state supplied by the adjacent supported machine. A pending job may still count as work while blocked or paused. Use the machine interface to find the reason it is not progressing.

Choose the variant for the intended neighboring machine. Availability and the exact work state depend on that machine.
buildcraftcore/trigger/machine_inactive: Has the machine finished its work?
Work Done checks the work state of an adjacent compatible machine.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Work Done is not proof that a production line delivered the desired result. Check the machine output and any missing-input state.

This is the opposite of the supported machine Has Work result. It can mean the current job is finished, but may also mean no job is configured or currently available. It is not a general detector for an unpowered machine.

Choose the variant for the intended machine and check its interface before using this as a completion signal.
buildcraftcore/action/redstone: Need a redstone signal without running another wire?
Redstone Signal is a Gate action that emits redstone power while its trigger is active.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Use Gate Side Only when only the face carrying the Gate should emit redstone.
While enabled, the Gate asks its pipe to emit redstone at strength 15. Use this to power a neighboring engine or a supported machine with a Redstone Controlling Module. It does not supply MJ.

Without a restriction, the output applies to the pipe sides. Gate Side Only restricts it to the physical face carrying the Gate. This is an action parameter, so it requires Quartz or Diamond support, not Lapis alone.
buildcraftcore/action/machine_control_on: Keep the machine running when the conditions are right.
On is a Gate action used to control an adjacent compatible machine.
<bold>Hint:</bold> A control mode can stay selected after its trigger becomes false. Configure an explicit opposite rule when the machine must return to another mode.

A mode command is not a universal engine switch and does not supply redstone or MJ. A Redstone Controlling Module, if installed, adds its own signal requirement; both controls must allow the job.
Select the action for the side occupied by the intended machine. If several active rows set modes for that same machine, the last matching rule wins. Avoid simultaneous On and Off commands.

buildcraftenergy/block/engine_stone: A furnace that moves a piston instead of cooking dinner is still a perfectly respectable furnace.
The Stirling Engine burns ordinary furnace fuels and produces between roughly 0.33 and 1 MJ per tick. In automatic FE compatibility modes that output may also feed compatible FE consumers.

Hint: Removing redstone prevents the next fuel item from starting, but the fuel already burning continues to run down. Keep a useful power outlet available during that time. Destructive overheating is controlled by engines.stirlingExplosion.

Place a valid furnace fuel in the single fuel slot and supply a redstone signal. The engine adjusts production between roughly 0.33 MJ/t and 1 MJ/t according to its stored energy; its internal buffer holds 1,000 MJ. A fuel item lasts for its normal furnace burn time.

<bold>Stopping:</bold> Removing redstone stops the next fuel item from being ignited. It does not freeze an item already burning: the burn timer continues, and that item can still generate MJ while the engine is below Overheat. Plan fuel supply and available buffer space accordingly. A returned container, such as an empty bucket, stays in the inventory when possible.

The guide uses per-tick rates. The live GUI may show the equivalent per-second rate when that display option is enabled.

Place the engine against an MJ receiver and use a Wrench to select the output face. Connect its output to a Wooden or Wooden Diamond Kinesis Pipe when feeding an MJ pipe network. The normal heat stages are blue, green, yellow, red and Overheat; Black is reserved for the Creative Engine. Stirling heat follows the fill level of the 1,000 MJ power buffer. A blocked output fills the buffer; at Overheat, generation stops, but the current fuel timer still runs down. The common setting engines.stirlingExplosion defaults to false; enabling it makes overheating destructive. Core power modes MJ_AUTOCONVERT_FE and DISPLAY_FE allow ordinary engine output to feed compatible FE consumers using the configured ratio. In MJ_ONLY, use the MJ Dynamo for explicit MJ-to-FE conversion.
buildcraftenergy/block/engine_iron: Burning refined fuel is a fine way to power a factory. Just remember to keep the engine cool.

The Combustion Engine burns liquid fuel to generate MJ. Fuel type and temperature determine power and heat; coolant and a residue outlet keep the engine operating. In Classic mode, Oil generates 3 MJ/t (30,000 MJ per bucket) and Fuel generates 6 MJ/t (600,000 MJ per bucket), without residue. Cooling and engine overheating still apply.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Test fuel, cooling, residue removal and automatic shutdown together. Hotter fuel gives more MJ per bucket but raises engine heat faster than it raises useful output.

The engine has three separate 10-bucket tanks: fuel, coolant and residue. Supply the correct fluids with pipes or containers, then apply redstone to burn fuel. Its energy buffer holds 10,000 MJ.

Crude Oil, Heavy Oil and Dense Oil are dirty fuels. Their residue must be drained: when the residue tank cannot accept the next by-product, the engine stops consuming more dirty fuel. Refined fuels do not produce residue. A residue outlet is therefore part of the fuel supply, not an optional cleanup step.

The fuel pages list the built-in MJ/t and MJ per bucket. The highest built-in output is Searing Gaseous Fuel at 12 MJ/t; the Cool version produces 8 MJ/t. Datapacks and addons can supply different fuel profiles.

Water is the standard coolant. Ice, Packed Ice and Blue Ice can be supplied as solid coolants; each item becomes 1,500, 2,000 or 3,000 mB of water respectively. This provides more coolant volume per item, rather than changing the cooling strength of each mB of water. Leave enough room in the coolant tank for the conversion.

The engine uses at most 40 mB of coolant per tick. Hot biomes increase heat production and reduce cooling effectiveness; colder biomes do the opposite. Supplying extra water faster than that internal limit cannot compensate for every high-heat setup. Monitor temperature under sustained load.

Removing redstone pauses combustion and starts a cooling lockout. Reapplying redstone does not bypass it: the engine must cool to its minimum heat before the short restart delay can finish. Avoid rapid on/off control that repeatedly forces this cooldown.

Rotate the engine with a Wrench so the moving end faces an MJ consumer or a Wooden Kinesis input. Keep the output able to accept power and provide a shutdown condition before the engine reaches dangerous heat. A full power buffer is not a reason to leave fuel burning unattended.

If the engine stops, check redstone, the restart cooling lockout, the fuel type and temperature, available coolant, residue space and the output connection.

Automatic FE compatibility in Core power mode can expose ordinary engine output to FE consumers at the configured ratio. The FE Engine converts FE to MJ; the MJ Dynamo converts MJ to FE. These are separate conversion blocks.

For every built-in burnable oil product, Cool is the baseline. Hot fuel produces 125% of the Cool output and Searing fuel produces 150%. Burn duration and residue per bucket stay the same, so total MJ per bucket rises by the same factors.

Heating rises more sharply: Hot fuel produces 150% and Searing fuel produces 200% of the Cool fuel's engine heat per tick. For example, Cool Oil gives 3 MJ/t and 30,000 MJ per bucket; Hot gives 3.75 MJ/t and 37,500 MJ; Searing gives 4.5 MJ/t and 45,000 MJ. The hotter variants need a stronger cooling plan.

These figures describe energy from burning the fuel. They do not subtract the energy and materials used to refine or heat it. Cool, Hot and Searing are separate fluid variants; empty the old fluid from a pipe or tank before switching that line to another temperature.
buildcraftfactory/block/distiller: Crude oil is a complicated collection of useful fluids waiting for someone to separate them.

The Distiller uses MJ to split a feed fluid into two products. The recipe is selected by both the fluid and its temperature. In Classic oil industry mode (World configuration > Operating Modes > Oil Industry), the Distiller acts as a refinery: 8 mB of Oil becomes 8 mB of Fuel for 32 MJ, with only the liquid output used. All fractionation routes below apply to Modern mode only.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Build and test both output lines before starting the feed. A full or contaminated output tank stops the entire recipe, even when the other product has plenty of room.

Feed the source fluid through a horizontal face. Extract the lighter product from the top and the heavier product from the bottom. Each internal tank holds four buckets. Use separate tanks and pipes for the two products; the top port is the recipe's lighter-output port even when that product is called an oil or a mixed fuel.

The Distiller does not push its outputs out by itself. With BuildCraft pipes, fit a powered Wooden Fluid Pipe or Diamond Wooden Fluid Pipe to each output. Ordinary transport pipes alone do not extract fluid. Supply MJ to the machine as well as to the extraction pipes. The default processing limit is 6 MJ/t; server balance settings and addons can change effective rates.

Cool, Hot and Searing variants are separate recipe inputs. Heating a fluid can change which products the Distiller makes; it is not merely a speed upgrade. Both products keep the feed's heat tier. Use a Heat Exchanger when the next refining stage requires a different tier.

For example, the bundled Cool Crude Oil recipe processes 8 mB into 16 mB of Gaseous Fuel and 3 mB of Heavy Oil for 32 MJ. Processing one bucket therefore yields two buckets of Gaseous Fuel and 375 mB of Heavy Oil for 4,000 MJ. Output volume can increase during separation, so size the gas storage accordingly. These are default recipe values; datapacks can replace them.

1. Pump Crude Oil into a buffer tank, then extract it into a horizontal Distiller face.

2. Supply MJ to the Distiller. Send the top output to a Gaseous Fuel tank and the bottom output to a separate Heavy Oil tank. Power both extraction connections.

3. Confirm that both tanks are filling before adding another refining stage. To refine the Heavy Oil further, first heat it to a temperature with a matching recipe. Feeding Cool Heavy Oil straight into another Distiller will not start a recipe.

4. If processing stops, check input temperature and quantity, MJ supply, both output tanks and both extraction pipes. Adding engines cannot fix a blocked output or an input with no recipe.
buildcraftfactory/block/heat_exchange: Some recipes need heat; others have too much of it. A Heat Exchanger can help with both.

The Heat Exchanger transfers heat between two fluid streams. It can heat one BuildCraft fluid while cooling another and does not require MJ. Classic mode disables the built-in oil and fuel temperature recipes; non-petroleum heat exchange recipes remain available.

<bold>Hint:</bold> Identify the two end sections by their vertical ports: the bottom inlet receives the fluid to heat, while the top outlet releases the heated product. The hotter supply enters the other end horizontally.

Place three to five Heat Exchanger blocks in one straight horizontal row, with matching orientation. The machine forms a start section, one to three middle sections and an end section. Two blocks are insufficient; a row longer than five is not a larger valid exchanger. More middle sections increase throughput.

Use the Wrench to change orientation. When a complete exchanger is rotated, its start and end swap, so recheck all four connections before reconnecting a running refinery.

<bold>Fluid to heat:</bold> insert it under the start section. Its heated product comes out above the end section.

<bold>Fluid to cool:</bold> insert it through the outer horizontal port of the end section. Its cooled product comes out of the outer horizontal port of the start section. The streams cross the machine; an output beside an input does not necessarily belong to that input.

Both inputs need matching heating/cooling recipes, and the cooling stream must start hotter than the heating stream. Keep room for both products. A machine full of equally hot fluids cannot transfer useful heat merely because both tanks are filled. The exchanger automatically offers its products to the connected output handlers.

To cool Hot oil or fuel, feed it into the horizontal cooling inlet and feed Water into the bottom heating inlet. Collect the Cool oil or fuel from the opposite horizontal outlet. In the bundled recipes, the Water is consumed and produces no fluid output; an empty top output is normal in this setup.

To heat oil using Lava, put oil in the bottom heating inlet and Lava in the horizontal cooling inlet. Collect heated oil from the top outlet. The bundled Lava recipe consumes the Lava without producing another fluid. Keep both supplies replenished.

For heat recovery, replace the consumable Water or Lava stream with a compatible oil product at a suitable temperature. One pass changes a BuildCraft oil product by one heat tier: Cool to Hot or Hot to Searing, or the reverse when cooling. A two-tier change needs another pass. Recipe amounts and eligible fluids may be changed by datapacks.
buildcraftfactory/block/tank: Sooner or later, carrying every bucket by hand stops being a practical storage system.
Tanks store fluids in place and can be stacked into tall storage columns.
<bold>Hint:</bold> A tank stores fluid but does not power an extraction pipe. Use a powered Wooden Fluid Pipe when you want to draw from it into a BuildCraft pipe line.

Each Tank block holds up to 16 buckets of one fluid. Stack Tanks vertically to share storage with the blocks above and below; adjacent columns remain separate. Keep each column dedicated to one fluid, including its temperature variant.

Connect a supply pipe or fluid container to fill the column. Connect a powered extraction pipe to draw fluid back out. If a line refuses to fill a partly empty column, check whether the column already contains a different fluid or heat variant.

Breaking a Tank does not keep the fluid inside the tank item itself. Instead, its stored fluid is converted into <bold>Fragile Fluid Shards</bold>. Use the shards on compatible fluid storage to recover it. Collect those drops promptly before dismantling more tanks. A vertical tank column still stores up to 16 buckets per tank block.
buildcraftfactory/block/pump: The collection of fluids by hand can be tedious, dangerous and very bad for shoes.

The Pump collects reachable world fluids, stores them internally and pushes them into adjacent tanks or fluid pipes. It can also drain thick fluid obstructing a Quarry when mounted directly on top of it.

<bold>Hint:</bold> For a first water supply, place the Pump above a renewable pool, connect a fluid output and give it MJ. For an oil deposit under water, keep the shaft clear: reachable non-water fluids are considered before Water.

Place a Pump above the target fluid with an unobstructed vertical shaft, then supply MJ. The tube searches down the passable column and also checks fluids beside it. Solid obstructions stop the shaft; the Pump does not drill through stone to find hidden oil.

The Fluid Scan Range setting limits how far the connected-fluid search may travel from the selected intake in any direction. Its default is 64 blocks, with a configurable range of 16 to 128. Unloaded chunks are not pulled in merely to continue the scan. The search proceeds over several ticks on large fluid bodies.

Collected fluid is automatically offered to adjacent fluid handlers. A normal fluid transport pipe can carry that output; no separate extraction engine is needed there. Default internal storage is 16 buckets and base extraction cost is 10 MJ per bucket, before balance multipliers. Drain the output continuously: the Pump pauses collection when its internal tank is more than half full.

By default, Consume Water Sources is disabled. The Pump preserves a recognised renewable Water source while producing Water. Enabling the setting makes it drain source blocks normally, although the world may still regenerate Water by its usual rules. Other fluids are removed from the world. These settings are in the BCCE configuration editor under the Pump's machine balance options.

Without a Redstone Controlling Module, ordinary redstone does not switch the Pump off. With a module installed, the Pump runs only while receiving a redstone signal. A Pump attached to a Quarry also respects the Quarry's module control.

1. Place the Pump directly on top of the Quarry block, not over the visible drill. Connect a separate fluid output and storage.

2. Supply the Pump with MJ. It can also draw unused energy from an idle Quarry when both machines have the same owner; a separate supply is useful while the Quarry still has other work.

3. When thick fluid such as Lava or Crude Oil blocks a mining column, the attached Pump targets that fluid instead of searching below its own block. Once the obstruction is drained, the Quarry rechecks the column and can continue downward.

4. If nothing moves, check fluid output capacity, available MJ, ownership for shared power, permissions and any installed redstone modules. A hosted Pump does not extend an ordinary tube through the Quarry block.
buildcraftfactory/block/flood_gate: Buckets are excellent for one hole. They become less charming when the hole is an artificial lake.
The Flood Gate accepts fluid and places full source blocks into reachable empty space without consuming MJ.

<bold>Hint:</bold> Fill a small enclosed basin first. Close the faces that lead outside it before supplying fluid; the Flood Gate searches reachable space rather than only the block immediately in front of it.

Pipe fluid into the Flood Gate or use a compatible fluid container. It keeps a two-bucket tank and needs a full bucket before placing a source block. No MJ is required.

Use a Wrench on a horizontal face or the bottom face to toggle that face open or closed. The top face is not a selectable world-placement opening. Open faces seed the fill search; closing one does not create a physical dam.

A redstone signal pauses placement. This is the Flood Gate's own control and does not require a Redstone Controlling Module. Normal liquids search downward and sideways; lighter-than-air fluids search upward and sideways.

The search radius is 64 blocks and placement stays within loaded, reachable space. Sealed walls block the search, and protection rules can reject placement. The scan is incremental, so a large basin may take time to discover and fill.

If the tank is full but no block appears, check the redstone signal, open faces, space reachable from those faces and whether that fluid can be placed in the world. Supplying a fluid used only in machines does not guarantee it has a placeable source block.
buildcraftfactory/block/mining_well: Sometimes the shortest route to a resource is still a perfectly vertical hole.
The Mining Well digs a single column below itself, places its tube through the shaft and outputs the drops it can legally mine.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Connect output storage before supplying MJ. The Mining Well can eject unaccepted drops; a full chest is not a reliable stop switch.

Place the Mining Well over the column you want to excavate. Supply MJ and connect an adjacent inventory or item transport line for the drops. The machine builds a tube into the cleared shaft; supply no separate tube items.

It skips standalone Water while searching downward, but unbreakable blocks, protected blocks and thick fluids such as Lava can prevent progress below them. It does not turn every obstruction into a mineable block. Use a separate Pump to remove a fluid obstruction when necessary.

Harder blocks require more MJ. Maximum Mining Depth in the BCCE configuration editor limits the vertical reach, and the world's build-height limits still apply. The default depth limit is 256 blocks below the machine.

Ordinary redstone does not pause an unmodified Mining Well. Install a Redstone Controlling Module if you want lever or gate control: with the module fitted, a signal is required to run.

When a well stops, inspect the first remaining block or fluid in its shaft, then check MJ, protection permissions and the module signal. Protection checks use the machine owner identity. More engines cannot overcome bedrock or a denied block-break action.
buildcraftfactory/block/chute: Sometimes all an inventory needs is a convenient way to move items along.
The Chute collects dropped items and moves them into connected inventories or out into the world, depending on its orientation.

<bold>Hint:</bold> The facing side is the pickup side; the other five sides are outputs. Put the receiving inventory beside an output face rather than covering the opening you want to collect through.

The Chute picks up loose item entities through its <bold>facing side</bold>. It then tries to transfer stored items through the other five sides into compatible inventories, entities or pipes. It does not extract inventory contents through the pickup opening.

For a simple collection point, face the Chute upward, leave its top open and attach storage below or beside it. Items dropped over the opening can enter without a Wooden Pipe extraction setup.

Each pickup cycle requires work. Facing upward provides a small amount of free gravity progress, so the Chute can collect slowly without external MJ. External MJ accelerates it; other facing directions require MJ for loose-item pickup. A Redstone Engine is suitable for light-duty collection.

If items remain above the opening, check the facing, MJ for non-upward pickup, and whether the Chute has room. If it holds items but cannot empty, inspect the receiving sides and the destination's insertion rules.
buildcraftfactory/block/auto_workbench: As with every engineer's duty, you eventually find a reason to automate the crafting table as well.
The Auto Workbench stores a recipe, accepts ingredients from automation and crafts it repeatedly. It works slowly by itself and can use MJ to accelerate progress.
<bold>Hint:</bold> The recipe grid stores a pattern. Put real ingredients in the material inventory and keep the output clear; putting an item into a phantom slot does not supply it for crafting.

Set a crafting recipe in the phantom grid, then supply actual ingredients to the material slots or pipe them in. The material inventory filters incoming items according to the selected recipe. Finished crafts appear in the output slot, which automation can extract. The Recipe Book can fill the phantom grid directly without consuming ingredients.

If several recipes match the same phantom grid, left-click the recipe output selector for the next recipe or right-click for the previous one; the choice is saved. Check the displayed output before connecting a continuous ingredient supply.

Each craft requires 40 MJ of progress. With ingredients and output room available, the workbench generates 0.2 MJ/t by itself: about ten seconds per craft at normal tick speed. External MJ speeds this up. Progress decays while the craft cannot proceed, so a blocked output or missing ingredient can also lose accumulated progress.

Automatic FE conversion can supply its MJ receiver when the server's power mode permits it. Check the actual power mode before assuming an FE cable can power any MJ machine.

If the preview is correct but crafting stalls, check every required ingredient, the selected alternative recipe, crafting remainders and output space before increasing power.
buildcraftlib/config/registry_overview: The guide registry is the table of contents behind the book: it decides what exists, where it appears and which icon represents it.
This page describes the language-neutral Guide Book manifest used by BuildCraft Community Edition.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Keep page IDs stable after release; changing the display text is safe, while changing an ID can invalidate saved book history and external links.
Every entry has an id and a language-neutral page key. Optional fields define module, type, subtype, display-name fallback, book, listing state, item stack, NBT variant, statement and required mod.

The built-in manifest never contains translated prose. Page mechanics live in page_layouts.json; English and translated strings live in the files under text/. Resource packs can replace those built-in layers independently, while addons can contribute sections, entries and pages through Guide API2 without replacing BuildCraft resources.
Every manifest page key must exist in the shared layouts and in the default English text pack. Translations may omit pages or individual slots when a fallback is configured.
buildcraftlib/config/json_insn_format: Data-driven instructions are useful when a resource pack must adjust a registry without compiling Java code.
This technical page summarizes the legacy BuildCraft JSON instruction language retained for resource compatibility.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Prefer the packed manifest and text resources for new Guide Book pages; use instruction scripts only when modifying a legacy registry script.
Instruction files start with the marker below. Imported library files use ~{buildcraft/json/lib} instead and may declare an argument count with ~args N.
The parser accepts comments and function calls such as add, remove, replace, modify, overwrite, alias and import. Arguments may be numbers, quoted strings or backtick-delimited multi-line strings.

The Community Edition guide no longer loads one Markdown file per entry. Index metadata is in original_manifest.json, shared templates are in page_layouts.json, and translated slot arrays are in text/<language>.json.
buildcraftlib/config/guide_page_format: A guide page stays maintainable when mechanics and translations are not copied into every language.
This page describes the packed, localized Guide Book resource format used by BuildCraft Community Edition.
<bold>Hint:</bold> After changing a layout, test both Lore and Hints settings and open the page in English and at least one translated language.

Language-neutral page structure is stored once in assets/buildcraft/guide/page_layouts.json. Each page has a Markdown template and numbered {{bc_text:index}} slots. Recipes, links, images, visibility tags and other mechanics belong in the template.

Visible text is stored in one compact file per language under assets/buildcraft/guide/text/<language>.json. A page value is an array whose indexes match the template slots. This keeps technical structure out of translations and lets the whole language compress as one JAR entry.

assets/buildcraft/guide/languages.json selects the default language, regional aliases and fallback chains. A missing page or a null slot inherits its parent language; an empty string intentionally hides that slot.

original_manifest.json contains the built-in index metadata: page ID, page key, module, type, subtype, visibility and optional item or statement references. The page key connects an entry to its layout and localized text. Addons do not need to replace this file: Guide API2 sections and entries are merged into the same runtime contents and search index.
Normal Markdown text, headings and formatting tags are supported. The tags below are language-neutral and should remain in the shared layout.
buildcraftsilicon/item/plug_facade: Pipes are useful. A wall full of exposed pipes is not always the look you had in mind.
Facades cover pipe faces with the appearance of a selected block, helping your machinery blend into a build.

Hint: Facades are enabled by default. Servers can disable creation and placement of new facades with facades.enable; facades already placed in a world are preserved so existing builds are not corrupted.

Almost any supported block state can be made into a facade and placed on the side of a pipe. A solid Facade blocks a pipe connection through that face, while a Hollow Facade allows the connection to pass through. The common Silicon setting facades.enable defaults to true. When disabled, new facades cannot be placed or produced by the normal facade recipes/Assembly Table paths, but already installed facades continue to load and render.
buildcraftsilicon/item/plug_gate: Why build a redstone contraption the size of a house when a Gate can fit the logic on a pipe?
A Gate is an upgradable pipe pluggable that connects triggers to actions, letting you automate pipes and nearby machines.

<bold>Hint:</bold> A robot station needs action parameters. Choose Quartz or Diamond, not Lapis alone. A Gold Quartz Gate has four rows with one parameter on each side; this is a useful starting point for a robot home station.
Gate Placement

Attach the Gate to a free face of a pipe, then right-click the Gate itself. The Gate blocks normal pipe connections through its own face. A Docking Station, Pulsar or Sensor goes on a different free face of the <bold>same pipe block</bold>.

A Gate can inspect that pipe, its attached pluggables and supported blocks directly beside it. It does not discover a remote chest just because a pipe network reaches it. Place a second Gate at the remote location and carry a signal with Pipe Wire when needed.
Gate Tiers

Material determines the number of rows before modifiers:

Basic (Clay Brick): 1 row, no modifier.
Iron: 2 rows.
Nether Brick: 4 rows.
Gold: 8 rows.

One row contains a trigger and an action. More rows let you keep separate rules or combine several conditions. Material alone does not supply parameter slots.
Gate Modifiers

Lapis: 1 trigger parameter, no action parameters; keeps all rows.
Quartz: 1 trigger and 1 action parameter; halves the rows.
Diamond: 3 trigger and 3 action parameters; halves the rows.

For example, Iron Quartz has 1 row, Nether Brick Quartz has 2 and Gold Quartz has 4. Diamond provides more filters per row, not more rows. Basic Gates cannot be modified.

An action with a required parameter will be absent from the choices if the Gate has no action-parameter slots. This is why an unmodified Gold Gate can offer fewer robot controls than a smaller Quartz Gate.
Gate Variants

AND and OR operate on <bold>connected groups of rows</bold>. In an AND group every trigger must be true; in an OR group any true trigger enables the group. Every action in that group receives the same result.

Disconnected rows remain independent even in an AND Gate. Do not join unrelated rules such as a robot work filter and a wake-up condition merely because they belong to the same robot. An empty trigger in a connected AND group is false and prevents the entire group from running.
Triggers

Drag a trigger from the available choices into a left-hand row slot. Press and hold the left mouse button on an installed statement, move to the desired variant and release. Shift-left-click its slot to clear it.

Choices are grouped by the pipe center and by direction. If two chests touch the pipe, select the Inventory trigger for the intended chest face. For a Docking Station or Pulsar, select the face occupied by that pluggable. The face shown by the statement matters; the physical face carrying the Gate does not automatically select the target.
Actions

Drag the desired action into the right-hand slot of the row. The action runs when that row or its connected group is enabled. Active indicators let you check the condition before relying on the machine.

Different actions have different lifetimes. Redstone and wire outputs require an active rule. A setting such as a pipe direction or machine mode can remain at its last value after the trigger stops. Add an explicit opposite or reset rule when the machine must return to another state.
Parameters

To set an item parameter, pick up the reference item in your inventory and click the small parameter slot beside the statement. It stores a <bold>copy</bold>; the real item stays on your cursor. Click an item parameter with an empty cursor to clear it. For an option parameter, press and hold, move to the desired option in the selector and release.

The parameter is an instruction, not a supply slot. A pickaxe copied into a robot Tool Filter does not give that robot a pickaxe. Supply the actual tool through an item-provider station. Changing a List or Map Location later does not update copies already stored in Gates.

Read the individual action page: a block sample, filled fluid container, List, robot item and Map Location have different meanings. Lists are accepted only by statements that explicitly support them.
Connections

Click the connector between neighboring rows to join or separate their condition groups. To test a simple rule, leave all connectors off and use Always On in its trigger slot.

Example: to run an action only when a lever is on <bold>and</bold> a chest has space, put Redstone Signal On in one row and Space in Inventory for that chest in the next, join those two rows in an AND Gate, and put the desired action in either row. All actions in the joined pair will run together.

If several active rows write the same setting for the same target, the last matching row wins. Avoid conflicting rules; do not expect repeated copies of one filter action to combine automatically.

Robot area actions share one setting family in the current Gate logic: Work in Area and Load/Unload in Area in the same Gate override one another. To keep different work and logistics boundaries, put those actions in two Gates on the home pipe. A simpler setup can use only Work in Area with one map that includes both the work patch and its service stations.
First Working Extraction Rule

1. Put a Wooden Transport Pipe against a chest and use a Wrench until its extraction face points at the chest. Connect a normal item pipe to an output face and lead it to another chest.

2. Fit a Pipe Pulsar and a Gate on two remaining faces of the Wooden Pipe. Leave the Pulsar manual switch off.

3. Set one independent row to Always On -> Power Pulsar On, choosing the Pulsar face. Items should now leave the source chest. Replace Always On with Redstone Signal On to control extraction with a lever.

4. A source-side Gate cannot see the destination chest through the pipe run. To stop on destination fill, put another Gate beside that chest, broadcast its Space in Inventory result on a chosen Pipe Wire color, and use that wire signal at the extractor.
When a Rule Does Nothing

Missing action: check Gate modifier, pipe type, attached pluggable and selected side; reopen the Gate after changing the surrounding blocks.

Dark trigger: check the exact condition, side and parameter. A filled container selects a fluid; an empty bucket does not.

Lit action, idle machine: check real power, materials, output space and machine enable controls. For robots, also check the home station, station access, work area, logistics area and sleep state.

Unexpected behavior: disconnect unrelated rows, remove competing actions, turn off manual Pulsar mode and test one rule at a time.
buildcraftsilicon/item/plug_pulsar: Sometimes all a pipe needs is a quick pulse of MJ rather than an entire engine.
A Pipe Pulsar supplies small MJ pulses to compatible extraction pipes without a separate engine.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Right-click toggles continuous manual operation. Switch that mode off before testing automatic Gate shutdown; manual operation can keep the Pulsar running after the Gate turns off.

Fit the Pulsar on a compatible Wooden item or fluid extraction pipe, leaving the extraction and output faces free. A normal right-click toggles manual continuous operation; it is not a single pulse.

A Gate on the same pipe can select Power Pulsar On for continuous pulses or Single Power Pulse for one activation. Select the statement for the Pulsar face. Continuous operation supplies 1 MJ per pulse, one pulse every 20 running ticks. It is useful for extraction, not as a general factory power source.

The Pulsar occupies and blocks its pipe face. A Gate must use another face. If nothing moves, check the Wooden Pipe extraction direction, the source inventory or tank, and the outgoing route before adding more power.
buildcraftsilicon/item/plug_light_sensor: Daylight is a perfectly good redstone input when you know how to measure it.
A Light Sensor measures the block immediately in front of its pipe face and adds Bright and Dark triggers to Gates on that pipe.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Torches and other local light sources can affect the reading. Use the exact Sensor face in the Gate when more than one sensor is installed.

Attach the Sensor to the face pointing toward the block to measure. Bright is active at light level 8 or above; Dark is active below 8. The measurement includes local lighting and the current sky darkening, so the Sensor is not just a day/night clock.

Install a Gate on another face of the same pipe and select the Bright or Dark variant for this Sensor.
The Sensor blocks its pipe face. Leave the transport faces clear and use a different free face for the Gate.
buildcraftsilicon/item/plug_lens: A traveling item can carry a routing color without changing the item you eventually take out of the chest.
A Lens paints items as they cross its pipe face. A Filter checks that transport color. Both use colored variants of the Lens item.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Pipe paint, traveling-item color and Pipe Wire color are separate systems. Use a Lens with Filters or color-routing pipes to build an item sorting network.

Attach a colored Lens to an item-pipe face. Items crossing that face in either direction acquire the Lens color. The color belongs to the item while it travels through the pipe; it does not dye the item itself or select an item type.

The Lens does not require a Gate or Pipe Wire signal and does not display a wire signal. It keeps the pipe connection open.

A Filter is the filtering variant of the same item. It favors items already painted its color, rejects items painted a different color and leaves an unpainted route available at lower priority.

For example, paint a batch red with a red Lens, then use a red Filter on the intended branch. The Filter does not recognize iron, wood or any other material by itself; use a Diamond Pipe or another item filter when the item type matters.
buildcraftsilicon/trigger/light_high: Is the area in front of the Light Sensor bright?
Bright is a Gate trigger that uses a Light Sensor attached to the same pipe.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Connect the trigger to a temporary lamp first. Once its active and inactive states are confirmed, route the same signal to machinery.

The trigger checks the light level in the block immediately in front of the selected Light Sensor and is active at a level 8 or above. Local block light and sky darkening both affect the result.

The Sensor and Gate must be on the same pipe. Choose the sided trigger for that Sensor, rather than assuming the Gate face is the measured direction.
buildcraftsilicon/trigger/light_low: Is the area in front of the Light Sensor dark?
Dark is a Gate trigger that uses a Light Sensor attached to the same pipe.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Connect the trigger to a temporary lamp first. Once its active and inactive states are confirmed, route the same signal to machinery.

The trigger checks the light level in the block immediately in front of the selected Light Sensor and is active at a level below 8. Local block light and sky darkening both affect the result.

The Sensor and Gate must be on the same pipe. Choose the sided trigger for that Sensor, rather than assuming the Gate face is the measured direction.
buildcraftsilicon/action/pulsar_constant: A Gate can switch an attached Pipe Pulsar on without a separate redstone circuit.
Power Pulsar On is a Gate action that enables a Pipe Pulsar on the same pipe.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Disable the Pulsar manual switch when the Gate should have sole control. An inactive Gate does not cancel a manually enabled Pulsar.

While this action remains enabled, the selected Pulsar runs continuously, giving its extraction pipe a 1 MJ pulse every 20 running ticks. Always On creates continuous extraction; Redstone Signal On lets a lever enable it.

When the rule stops, the automatic enable has a short grace period of up to 10 ticks. A pulse already underway or manual operation should not be confused with a failed trigger.
Choose the action variant for the face carrying the Pulsar. Several Pulsars on one pipe have separate sided action choices; a Gate on another pipe cannot directly operate them.
buildcraftsilicon/action/pulsar_single: One extraction pulse is sometimes all you need.
Single Power Pulse is a Gate action that briefly fires a Pipe Pulsar on the same pipe.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Use a Timer trigger or switch a lever off and on between activations. Always On queues one single pulse, not a repeating clock.

The transition from an inactive rule to an active rule queues one pulse. Holding the same condition true does not keep queuing pulses; the rule must become inactive before it can fire again.

The Pulsar completes the pulse after its running cycle. For item extraction the pulse is budgeted for one item; for fluid extraction it is budgeted for 1,000 mB using the current extraction energy cost. Available contents, pipe space and flow limits still apply, so this is not a guarantee that a full bucket arrives instantly.
Choose the action for the Pulsar face. Keep manual mode off when testing single pulses, otherwise manual continuous pulses will also power the pipe.
buildcrafttransport/pipe/structure: A pipe network can carry signals even where it does not need to carry items.
Structure Pipes hold Pipe Wire, Gates and other pluggables without transporting items, fluids or energy.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Structure Pipes are useful mounting points for wires, gates and plugs where no item transport is required.

Just like a normal pipe, Pluggables and Pipe Wires can be placed on it without carrying items, fluids, MJ or FE.

Pipe holders in current BuildCraft versions are waterloggable. A pipe placed into water can preserve the water in its block space instead of requiring the network to drain the area first. This applies to transport pipes as well as Structure Pipes.
buildcrafttransport/pipe/wood_item: Need to get items out of a chest automatically? Start with a Wooden Transport Pipe.
A Wooden Transport Pipe uses MJ pulses to extract items from an adjacent inventory.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Build and test the destination before powering extraction. A Wooden Pipe can keep extracting even when a distant chest is full.

Place the pipe against the source inventory. Its solid extraction end must face the inventory; use a Wrench on the required side, or cycle valid sides from the center. Attach a normal item pipe to carry the output to a destination. Wooden extraction pipes do not connect directly to one another.

The source must allow extraction from the face used. A machine may expose input slots on one side and output slots on another. This is separate from sorting farther down the pipe. Items with no permitted route can fall into the world, so provide an overflow or stop extraction when storage fills.
A connected MJ engine, Power Adapter or Pipe Pulsar can power extraction.

At default balance, extraction costs 1 MJ per item. A sufficiently large pulse can extract multiple items, subject to what the source exposes. Ordinary redstone alone supplies no MJ: use an engine, a powered connection through a Power Adapter, or an active Pipe Pulsar. Some machines push items into pipes directly and need no extraction pulse.
buildcrafttransport/pipe/cobble_item: Simple item transport with plenty of friction along the way.
Cobblestone Transport Pipes move items through a network and slow fast-moving items.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Use Cobblestone and Stone pipes together when adjacent lines must remain separate without paint or plugs.

The Cobblestone Transport pipe gives transported items a high amount of drag so they will slow accelerated items quickly.

Cobblestone Transport pipes will not connect to Stone or Quartz Transport Pipes.

If the pipe has multiple connecting sides, the items will travel toward a valid output.
Items normally continue forward rather than immediately reversing into the pipe they came from.
If there is nowhere for the moving items to go, they will be dropped out of the pipe onto the ground.

Some machines insert items directly into connected pipes without a powered extraction pipe.
Using Pipe Plugs or painting pipes a different color can stop pipes connecting.
buildcrafttransport/pipe/stone_item: Stone makes a good general-purpose route for transported items.
Stone Transport Pipes move items through a network with moderate drag.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Use Stone and Cobblestone pipes together when adjacent lines must remain separate without paint or plugs.

The Stone Transport pipe gives transported items a medium amount of drag so they will slow accelerated items.

Stone Transport pipes will not connect to Cobblestone or Quartz Transport Pipes.

If the pipe has multiple connecting sides, the items will travel toward a valid output.
Items normally continue forward rather than immediately reversing into the pipe they came from.
If there is nowhere for the moving items to go, they will be dropped out of the pipe onto the ground.

Some machines insert items directly into connected pipes without a powered extraction pipe.
Using Pipe Plugs or painting pipes a different color can stop pipes connecting.
buildcrafttransport/pipe/quartz_item: For a longer run, it helps when the pipes do not slow your items quite so much.

buildcrafttransport/pipe/diamond_item: One chest for stone and another for diamonds? Now you are thinking like an engineer.
A Diamond Transport Pipe routes items to different outputs according to its side filters.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Leave an unfiltered side only when it is intended as overflow. Filtered sides take priority, so test scarce items before connecting bulk traffic.

Open the GUI and match each row color to the colored face on the pipe. Click items into the phantom slots to set filters; these are samples, not stored cargo. A List can match a larger group of items.

A matching filtered side has priority over an unfiltered side. A side with filters rejects items matching none of them. Leave one unfiltered route for intentional overflow.

<bold>Weighted splitting:</bold> The quantities of matching samples determine the ratio between eligible filtered outputs. Two matching samples on one side and one on another give a 2:1 weighting. Larger stacks can be divided in that ratio; leftover items are distributed using those weights. This is item routing: repeating a fluid filter in a Diamond Fluid Pipe does not create the same weighting.

Example: connect one chest to the red face and another to the blue face. Put cobblestone in the red filter and iron ingots in the blue filter; connect an unfiltered third side to a miscellaneous chest. Send a small test stack of each item before enabling bulk extraction.

Filters select permitted routes; they do not reserve room in the destination. A blocked or full destination can cause retries, another eligible route or item ejection. Provide capacity and an overflow instead of treating the pipe as storage.
buildcrafttransport/pipe/obsidian_item: Dropped items do not have to stay on the ground. Let a pipe collect them.
An Obsidian Transport Pipe picks up loose items and sends them into an item pipe network.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Power improves collection behavior. Place the pipe where loose items cannot be pulled from areas that players still use manually.

Without MJ, loose items are collected only when they physically touch the pipe. When powered, the pipe searches outward from its open face. The powered search extends up to four blocks and widens with distance instead of using a fixed box above the pipe. More distant items require more MJ to pull in.

The Obsidian Pipe needs exactly one connected transport side to establish its pickup face; the pickup face is opposite that connection. With zero or multiple connections there is no single open pickup face, so collection is disabled. Keep collection at an endpoint rather than at a junction.

If there is nowhere for the received items to go, they will be dropped out of the pipe onto the ground.
Using Pipe Plugs or painting pipes a different color can stop pipes connecting.
A compatible MJ source, such as an engine, Power Adapter or Pipe Pulsar, can power the pipe.

MJ pulses pay for powered pickup. Larger accepted pulses allow more items to be collected, including items farther from the pickup face. Unpowered contact pickup still requires a valid open face. The pipe will not immediately recollect an item it has just ejected, so a blocked output should be fixed rather than used as a collection loop.
buildcrafttransport/pipe/sandstone_item: A pipe next to a chest should not always connect to it.

<bold>Hint:</bold> Sandstone Pipes are useful beside dense machine walls because they avoid unwanted inventory connections. Confirm every intended endpoint remains connected.

buildcrafttransport/pipe/stripes_item: Why stop at moving blocks when a pipe could place or break them as well?
A Stripes Transport Pipe can interact with blocks in front of it, including placing and breaking blocks, when properly configured.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Use Stripes Pipes at controlled endpoints and test the target face manually. Their world interaction is more destructive than normal transport.

With a working face selected, the pipe uses stored MJ to break the block immediately in front of it and sends the drops into the pipe network. Breaking accumulates progress according to the block's required energy; a power pulse is not a promise to break a whole block instantly.

Items reaching the working endpoint are offered to Stripes interactions. Supported blocks can be placed and supported items can be used there. The exact interaction depends on the item and registered behavior; the pipe is not a universal substitute for every player right-click.

With one transport connection, the pipe automatically points toward the opposite open face. Multiple connections do not provide an automatic working direction. To choose a different open face explicitly, use a Face Direction action on a Gate attached to this pipe. The selected working face must remain unconnected and unobstructed by a blocking plug.

If there is nowhere for the traveling items to go, they will be dropped out of the pipe onto the ground.
Using Pipe Plugs or painting pipes a different color can stop pipes connecting.

MJ is stored and spent on the current block over time. A harder block needs more work, so watch breaking progress rather than counting pulses. Changing the target or direction resets that target's progress. Unloaded chunks, unbreakable blocks and protection rules can prevent work even when energy is available.
buildcrafttransport/pipe/diamond_wood_it: Extracting items is useful. Extracting only the ones you actually want is better.
A Wooden Diamond Transport Pipe extracts items from an adjacent inventory using configurable filters.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Configure the extraction filter before applying power. An empty or broad filter can drain an inventory much faster than expected.

Attach the solid input end to the source inventory and use a Wrench to choose another valid source side if needed. The filter affects powered extraction from that inventory. Items inserted into the pipe by a machine are not filtered by this extraction rule. Connect ordinary item pipes on the output side; wooden extraction pipes do not connect directly to each other.

The GUI has nine phantom filters and three modes. <bold>Whitelist</bold> extracts matching items; an entirely empty whitelist permits every item. <bold>Blacklist</bold> extracts items that match none of the filters; an empty blacklist blocks nothing. A List can stand in for several item types.

<bold>Round Robin</bold> selects one configured filter at a time and advances after a successful extraction. If the currently selected item is unavailable, the item version waits for that filter rather than skipping it. Use this to enforce a sequence only when every ingredient remains available.
A connected MJ engine, Power Adapter or Pipe Pulsar can power extraction.

This filtered item extractor takes one item per successful extraction call, costing 1 MJ at default balance. A bigger individual pulse does not turn that call into a full-stack extraction. Feed regular pulses and verify the selected filter when throughput stops.
buildcrafttransport/pipe/lapis_item: Give items a color and the rest of the network can decide where they belong.
A Lazuli Transport Pipe paints items passing through it with its selected color.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Keep color-based routing documented near the network. A paint change upstream can alter every later routing decision.

Items gain the selected routing color when they reach the pipe center. Use a Wrench to cycle colors; sneaking cycles backwards. A Paint Items Gate action can set a color directly. The color is a label on the travelling item, not a change to the item itself.

Use Lazuli to label a stream, then a Daizuli Pipe or colored Filter to route that label. For example, paint one input blue and let a blue Daizuli outlet send that stream to its destination. A colored Lens can also paint items as they pass its face.

Painting the <bold>pipe</bold> with a Paintbrush controls which adjacent pipes connect. Painting the <bold>travelling item</bold> controls color-sensitive routing. Those are different settings. Ordinary item routing still applies after painting, including possible ejection if no output is available.
buildcrafttransport/pipe/daizuli_item: Colored items are only useful for sorting once a pipe knows what the colors mean.
A Daizuli Transport Pipe directs items according to their painted color.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Use Daizuli routing together with a clear color convention. Reserve one color for overflow or unsorted items.

Items carrying the selected routing color may leave only through the chosen colored output. Items with a different color, including uncolored items, cannot use that output and continue through other eligible connections. Provide another route for those items.

Example: paint a stream blue with Lazuli or a blue Lens. Set a Daizuli outlet to blue and point that outlet at the destination. Add a separate route for other colors. A missing matching route can cause items to be ejected; color selection does not create a destination.

Use a Wrench on another connected side to make it the output. Click the center or the current output with a Wrench to cycle the color; sneaking reverses the color cycle. A Gate can set direction and color. These settings remain selected after the Gate condition stops, so add explicit actions for both states when automatic switching is required.
buildcrafttransport/pipe/emzuli_item: An extraction pipe with several filters is handy. One that a Gate can switch between is even better.
An Emzuli Transport Pipe extracts filtered items and uses Gate actions to select its extraction preset.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Emzuli needs both an active preset action and MJ. Choosing a filter in the GUI alone does not start extraction.

A powered extraction pipe pulls items from the adjacent inventory on its input side and sends them through its connected outputs. When more than one output is available, normal pipe routing determines the destination. Items with nowhere to go may be dropped into the world.

Machines can also insert items into a connected pipe without powering its extraction mechanism. Use Pipe Plugs or pipe colors to separate nearby networks.

The GUI has four preset filters, each with an optional paint color for extracted items. Put an item or a List in the preset you want to use. Attach a Gate to the same pipe and pair a condition with that preset's Extraction Preset action.

For a first test, use Always On to activate one populated preset, then supply MJ. To control it with a lever, replace Always On with Redstone Signal On. When the condition goes false the preset expires and extraction stops.

Several preset actions can be active together. The pipe cycles among active, nonempty presets after successful extractions. If the current preset has no matching item in the source, it waits; it does not invent an alternative item. A preset with no filter cannot extract anything.
A connected MJ engine, Power Adapter or Pipe Pulsar can power extraction.

At default balance the pipe spends 1 MJ for each extracted item. Its active preset chooses both the item filter and, if configured, the routing color. The color can be read by Daizuli Pipes or Filters farther down the line. Direct insertion by another machine bypasses this extraction step.
buildcrafttransport/pipe/wood_fluid: Moving fluids usually begins by extracting them from a tank.
A Wooden Fluid Pipe uses MJ to draw fluid from an adjacent tank or machine.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Connect extraction to only one intended tank or machine face and provide immediate downstream capacity. A backed-up line stops useful pumping.

Place the solid input end against the tank or machine face that exposes fluid extraction. Use a Wrench to choose the correct source when several are adjacent. Supply MJ and attach ordinary Fluid Pipes for the outgoing route. Wooden extraction pipes do not connect directly to one another.

A powered source such as a Pump can push fluid into pipes itself; a passive tank needs extraction. Fluid Pipes do not need an engine on every segment. Each line still needs a compatible receiving tank and enough room for the fluid.
It can receive power from any MJ power source such as: an engine, Power Adapter or Pipe Pulsar.

At default balance, powered extraction costs 0.001 MJ per mB, or 1 MJ per bucket. More MJ can draw a larger pulse, but the pipe's transfer rate and available capacity still limit sustained flow. Redstone by itself supplies no extraction energy.

Default transfer rate: 10 mB/t, or 0.2 buckets per second at 20 ticks per second. It scales with pipes.baseFluidRate, whose default is 10 mB/t. At default balance it has a one-bucket center and one-bucket sections in its connected arms, but carries only one fluid variant at a time. Drain it before changing fluid type or temperature.
buildcrafttransport/pipe/cobble_fluid: An ordinary fluid line does not need to be fast, just dependable.
Cobblestone Fluid Pipes transfer fluid through a pipe network at a low rate.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Use the Stone/Cobblestone non-connection rule to run separate fluid lines side by side without accidental mixing.

Cobblestone Fluid Pipes have a low fluid transfer rate and do not connect directly to Stone or Quartz Fluid Pipes.

When several destinations can accept fluid, the pipe distributes it among available outputs rather than immediately sending it back toward the source.

Some machines can push fluid directly into connected pipes. Pipe Plugs and pipe colors help keep separate lines from joining.

Default transfer rate: 10 mB/t, equivalent to 0.2 buckets per second at 20 ticks per second. Rates scale with pipes.baseFluidRate; the default base is 10 mB/t. buildcrafttransport/pipe/iron_fluid: Liquids obey gravity in the world. Inside pipes, an Iron Pipe tells them which way to go.

<bold>Hint:</bold> Check the one-way output after rotating the pipe. Directional mistakes can trap fluid in a branch that appears connected.

Fluid enters through the other connected sides and leaves through the clear selected output. Use a Wrench or a Gate direction action to change that output. An ordinary redstone signal does <bold>not</bold> rotate the pipe. The selected output face does not accept incoming fluid.

A direction action changes the saved setting; the previous direction is not restored automatically when its condition stops. Use a second explicit action for the other control state. A full output stops useful flow, so provide storage or stop extraction upstream.

buildcrafttransport/pipe/gold_fluid: When throughput matters, a Golden Fluid Pipe is the next upgrade.
Golden Fluid Pipes move fluids through a pipe network at a high rate.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Use higher-throughput sections near pumps and large tanks, but keep enough receiving capacity to absorb bursts.

Golden Fluid Pipes have a high fluid transfer rate. They distribute fluid among connected destinations that can accept it.

Some machines can push fluid directly into connected pipes. Use Pipe Plugs or pipe colors to prevent unwanted connections.

buildcrafttransport/pipe/diamond_fluid: Mixing all your fluids together is a good way to ruin a refinery.
Diamond Fluid Pipes sort fluids between outputs using container-based side filters.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Configure every used side before attaching multiple fluids. Reserve an explicit overflow route rather than relying on an empty filter by accident.

Each side has colored phantom filter slots. Put a filled bucket or another valid fluid container in a side's filter to allow that fluid. Empty containers and ordinary items do not define a fluid. A side with valid fluid filters rejects other fluids.

Matching filtered sides have priority over unfiltered sides. Repeating the same fluid in several slots does <bold>not</bold> add routing weight; one matching sample is enough. Hot and Cool versions of an oil product are different fluids, so use the sample for the temperature actually being transported.

Example: use a Cool Gaseous Fuel bucket on the route to its tank and a Cool Heavy Oil bucket on the heavy-oil route. Leave an unfiltered side only if it leads to deliberate overflow storage.

The sorter permits routes; it does not mix fluids or reserve tank capacity. A segment already holding another fluid must drain before it can accept a new one. Separate output lines are more reliable than alternately feeding several refinery products through one shared trunk.

<bold>Hint:</bold> Use Sandstone Fluid Pipes where nearby tanks should not connect automatically. Inspect each face after rebuilding the machine wall.

Use Pipe Plugs or pipe colors to keep neighboring routes separate.
